details: Assigned: build isolated comm_skeleton micro-benchmark to measure pure bookkeeping cost (CB ops, NoC issue, semaphores, mcast rendezvous, DEST sync) at 88/110/1 cores
dest_probe.cpp compute kernel used namespace NAMESPACE/MAIN; this repo uses Metal-2.0 style global void kernel_main() for compute too (see xstage_compute.cpp). Rewrote entry point.
smoke PASS on Blackhole 11x10 (110 cores). All 6 probes compile+run, mcast payload gate verified on 88 cores.
Moved repeat counts (N_ITERS/N_CMDS/XFER_BYTES/N_OPS/ROUNDS/PAYLOAD) to runtime args: ~5-9x fewer JIT builds and faithful to the op (its trip counts are runtime). Smoke+correctness still PASS.

Headline confirmed 2 samples, spread <=1.7%: NoC issue = 21.5 ns read / 26.7 ns write (L1 target, batched barrier), CORE-COUNT-INDEPENDENT. NOT 50-100 cycles; ~29-36 cycles @1.35GHz. Full mcast rendezvous @88 cores DEPTH_H=3 = 1552-1636 ns/round => 17.1 us per 11-round M-block with a 64B payload.

Team lead reports shared generated/profiler/ artifacts dir races between concurrent agents. My path is in-process ttnn.get_latest_programs_perf_data(), not CSV/mtime. Verifying whether it is backed by the shared CSV, then isolating TT_METAL_PROFILER_DIR and re-verifying headline numbers.

Isolated TT_METAL_PROFILER_DIR to experiment dir and re-ran every measured probe. ALL numbers reproduce (NoC issue 21.48/26.67 identical to 4 s.f.; CB 27.4-30.8; sem 14.8/26.7/167; incast 9.46 ns/atomic; DEST 13.7). Confirmed the bench never touched the shared CSV: it reads in-process MetalContext::profiler_state_manager via GetLatestProgramsPerfData. CORRECTION: 5-sample mcast focus shows DEPTH>1 rounds are intrinsically variable (8-36% spread); retracting the earlier 2-sample claim that DEPTH_H 3->2 is ~6% faster - ranges overlap. DEPTH=1 serial round is deterministic at 1854 ns (0.1%).
